correctness.rationale: Allowed words are exactly counted by \(\boldsymbol 1^{\mathsf T}(AB)^m\boldsymbol 1\). The two-step matrix restricts to the span of \(\boldsymbol 1,e_p\), with trace \(k^2-2+de\), determinant \((kd-1)(ke-1)\), and initial values \(N_0=k\) and \(N_1=k^3-2k+d\). Cayley–Hamilton yields all four rational forms; exact subtractions yield strictly positive coefficient differences and phase asymmetry; positive real characteristic roots and explicit inequalities yield three ordered escape rates; the binary repeated root yields \(2(m+1)\) words of length \(2m+1\). The bound \((k-1)S_{2m}/k\le S_{2m+1}\le S_{2m}\) connects all horizons. A separate standard-library checker exhaustively tests all digit quadruples for bases two through six, including brute word enumeration.

originality.rationale: The 2014 time-dependent-hole source uses sinusoidal moving or breathing boundaries, numerical Ulam approximations, and overlap heuristics, not the claimed exact time-alternating length-two cylinder generating functions. The 2012 static Markov-hole treatment and 2019/2022 fixed forbidden-cylinder correlation theory yield related methods, but their forbidden words act at every time rather than on opposite parities. Explicit implication comparisons were made to static survivors and nearby studies of periodic points and truncated transfer operators; none supplies all-base strict finite-horizon phase ordering, exact three-rate classification, and the binary double-root prefactor. Equivalence risk remains for unlocated temporal SFT results.
residual_risks: Unlocated research on time-periodic symbolic holes or cyclic adjacency products could supply an equivalent explicit result.
Classical phase augmentation and transfer-matrix techniques might make some aspects derivable from earlier general theorems even without an explicit published four-case statement.

value.rationale: The precise finite-time escape counts, strict phase-sensitive hierarchy and exactly three distinct asymptotic rates form a complete natural classification for the simplest genuine time-periodic Markov holes. For mixed-overlap types, phase reversal is invisible to exponential rate yet distinguishable by every positive finite even horizon; the binary case has a nontrivial polynomial prefactor, a structural boundary effect. The theorem supplies exact all-base behavior to compare against moving-hole approximations; this is more than a numerical instance or routine parameter substitution.
